core_workflow.description: Connect -> Create/Open Table -> Add Data -> Query. Both sync and async APIs available.
core_workflow.connect: db = lancedb.connect('/path/to/db')  # local directory, or S3/GCS URI

schema_with_embeddings.description: LanceDB's Pydantic-based schema auto-generates embeddings via the embedding registry.

recommended_for_this_repo.reason: Best quality-to-size ratio for small document collections. Free, local, no API keys. Good for English technical text.

alternatives.note: Slightly lower quality but very fast. Good default.
Better quality than L6, slightly slower.
Higher quality, 2x embedding size. Use if quality matters more than speed.

notes: Embeddings auto-generated on add() when using LanceModel schema
Query embeddings auto-generated on search() calls
Normalized embeddings used by default (recommended for cosine similarity)
No API keys needed - runs entirely locally
First run downloads model (~130MB for bge-small-en-v1.5)

dependencies: pip install torch  # CPU-only: pip install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
commercial_options_if_needed: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small (1536 dims, requires API key)
Cohere embed-english-v3.0 (1024 dims, requires API key)
Google text-embedding-004 (768 dims, requires API key)

estimate_for_this_repo.verdict: Negligible. Even with all documents indexed, total storage is under 5 MB. The Lance format is disk-efficient and columnar.

lance_format_notes: Uses Apache Arrow columnar format on disk
Supports zero-copy reads for fast access
Compression available but minimal benefit for pre-compressed embeddings
Lance v2.1 format is stable and production-ready

vector_search.returns: Results include selected columns plus '_distance' column (lower = more similar)

full_text_search.returns: Results include '_score' column (BM25 relevance score, higher = more relevant)

hybrid_search.default_reranker: RRFReranker (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) - combines vector and FTS scores
hybrid_search.notes: Scores are normalized to make vector and FTS results comparable

query_api.auto_detection: If input is str and FTS index exists, uses hybrid/fts. If input is list[float], uses vector search.

lancedb_native_hybrid.description: LanceDB has built-in hybrid search combining vector similarity + BM25 full-text search in a single query.
how_it_works: 1. Create both vector index and FTS index on the same table
2. Use query_type='hybrid' to run both searches simultaneously
3. Results are combined using a reranking algorithm (default: RRF)
rerankers: RRFReranker (default) - Reciprocal Rank Fusion, no model needed
CrossEncoderReranker - Uses cross-encoder model for reranking (higher quality, slower)
lancedb_native_hybrid.recommendation: Use RRFReranker for this repo - fast, no extra dependencies, good enough for ~120 docs

alongside_sqlite_fts5.approach: Use LanceDB for semantic search + hybrid search. Keep existing SQLite FTS5 for fast keyword lookups if already in use.
alongside_sqlite_fts5.recommended_strategy: Replace SQLite FTS5 with LanceDB's built-in FTS since LanceDB handles both vector and full-text natively. This avoids maintaining two separate search systems.
when_to_keep_sqlite: If SQLite is used for structured data beyond search (coordination system, etc.)
If existing code heavily depends on SQLite FTS5 queries
If you need transactional guarantees that SQLite provides

architecture_options.name: Option A: LanceDB-only (recommended)
architecture_options.description: Use LanceDB for all search (vector + FTS). SQLite remains for coordination/structured data only.
architecture_options.pros: Single search API, simpler code, built-in hybrid search
architecture_options.cons: Need to migrate any existing FTS queries

architecture_options.name: Option B: LanceDB + SQLite side-by-side
architecture_options.description: LanceDB for semantic search, SQLite FTS5 for keyword search, merge results in application code.
architecture_options.pros: No migration needed, can compare approaches
architecture_options.cons: Two systems to maintain, custom result merging logic

phase_1_mvp.description: Index knowledge base entries only. ~38 documents. Proves the concept.
steps: 2. Create indexer script that reads KB Markdown files
3. Parse YAML frontmatter + body text from each entry
4. Create LanceDB table with auto-embedding schema
6. Create FTS index on text column
7. Create search function that runs hybrid queries
8. Return results with source paths and relevance scores

schema.text: str (SourceField - concatenation of title + summary + body)
schema.title: str

phase_2_expansion.description: Add team logs, SOPs, and scripts. ~120 documents total.
phase_2_expansion.effort: ~50 additional lines (mostly parsing logic per source type)

phase_3_full.description: Add chunking for long documents, graph-based retrieval links, cross-reference scoring.
features: Chunk long documents (>2000 tokens) into overlapping segments
Use builds_on / related_to metadata for graph-aware reranking
Add recency scoring (newer entries ranked higher for same relevance)

minimal_integration.recommendation: Start with Phase 1 MVP. It covers the highest-value content (KB entries) with minimal code. Expand to Phase 2 once validated.

incremental_updates.approach: Use merge_insert() with entry_id as the merge key for upsert semantics.

add_new_entry.description: When a new KB entry is created, add it to the LanceDB table. Embeddings are auto-generated.

update_existing_entry.description: When a KB entry is modified, use merge_insert to upsert.

full_reindex.description: For bulk updates or schema changes, recreate the table with mode='overwrite'.

incremental_updates.fts_index_rebuild: After adding new data, the FTS index may need rebuilding: table.create_fts_index('text', replace=True). Native FTS supports incremental indexing; Tantivy-based does not.
automation_options: Git hook (post-commit): detect changed .md files, update LanceDB
Startup scan: compare file mtimes with last-indexed timestamps
Watch script: inotify-based watcher for real-time indexing
incremental_updates.recommendation: Use startup scan approach: on each search session start, check for new/modified files and upsert them. Simple, reliable, no daemon needed.

recommended_approach.summary: Deploy LanceDB as an embedded vector database alongside the existing SQLite coordination system. Use sentence-transformers for free local embeddings. Start with KB entries, expand to all document types.

architecture.embedding_model: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (384 dims, ~130MB download, runs on CPU)
architecture.coordination_db: SQLite (unchanged - continues to handle coordination, structured data)

implementation_plan.task: Create storage/scripts/semantic_search.py with LanceDB indexing + search
Index all 38 KB entries with auto-embedding
implementation_plan.effort: First run: ~30 seconds (model download + embedding generation)

implementation_plan.task: Create FTS index for hybrid search
Expand to team logs, SOPs, scripts
Add incremental update on startup (scan for changed files)

key_advantages: Zero infrastructure - embedded, no server needed
Free embeddings - sentence-transformers runs locally on CPU
Native hybrid search - vector + BM25 in one query, no custom merging
Tiny footprint - <5 MB storage for entire repo
Simple API - ~150 lines for full implementation
Compatible with existing SQLite coordination system

risks_and_mitigations.risk: sentence-transformers + torch is a large dependency (~500MB-2GB)
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use CPU-only torch to reduce size. Or use onnx runtime for smaller footprint.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Tantivy FTS index doesn't support incremental updates
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use native FTS (use_tantivy=False) or rebuild FTS index on changes (fast for <200 docs)

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Model download required on first run
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Cache model in a known location. Document the first-run behavior.
